attempts.summary: On node1, created user `datauser`, built a dedicated XFS filesystem (loopback image at /var/lib/quota-images/srv-data.img, 512M) mounted at /srv/data via /etc/fstab with the `usrquota` option, and set a 100MB (soft=hard) block quota for datauser via xfs_quota. Verified the kernel enforces the limit directly (writes fail with "Disk quota exceeded" exactly at 100MB), that the config survives a full node reboot (boot_id changed, confirming a real restart), and that enforcement still works identically afterward. Switched from ext4 quotas to XFS after discovering this kernel ships CONFIG_QUOTA_TREE only as an unavailable module, so ext4's userspace quota format could not activate ("Quota format not supported in kernel"); XFS quotas are built directly into the XFS driver (CONFIG_XFS_QUOTA=y) and worked without issue.
